chapter: Second interview: bass, Parker and Miles
title: Martin Williams, Jelly Roll Morton and Miles Davis again
summary: Mingus again claims priority on one-chord playing, citing the Charles Cros award; Bill Evans and Wynton Kelly taught Miles.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Yeah, right. So you don't figure as much can be done in terms of the music, in terms of upgrading --
for example, at the Smithsonian, Martin Williams has had -- I don't know if he still has it, but he used to have summer sessions, seminars, to try to upgrade the level of jazz criticism.

Yeah, well, (inaudible) how good he is, Martin Williams got in my way when I was coming up. I started playing one chord when nobody was doing it (inaudible) Jelly Roll Morton, I never even heard Jelly Roll Morton. I pretended to hear him because he said it. He said, well, Jelly Roll Morton did that in 1927. Fuck Jelly Roll Morton, man. I was doing it and he didn't pay any attention to me.
Then when Miles Davis came along and copies what I was doing, and stopped playing bebop -- that's all he was doing, playing bebop --
That was that Kind of Blue album, right, that Miles was doing?
The proof of the pudding was that the Charles de Cross -- you heard of that association in France?

Well, they gave me an award six years later when Miles Davis was doing the tune -- his bass on a tune I think called Celia. Gave my record six years before with Records, with all those tunes on it, the same award as Miles got.
Yeah, I see what you mean. I was going
to ask you about your impressions about certain people.
Miles used to laugh when he played one chord.

When Max brought him by to hear the band, that was the Bohemia, he said, man, what are you doing, playing one chord a whole hour? What are you doing with one chord? Next thing I know, he was doing it.
He learned from the best, those guys in my band, like Wynton Kelly and Bill Evans. They really (inaudible) some records with me. They showed him how to do it. And he got all the credit for that.
